ia.name: Scientific investigation

criteria.name: Research design
look: A focused research question naming the independent and dependent variables, with range and units
Physics background that leads to a testable relationship (ideally one you can linearize)
A method detailed enough to repeat, with controlled variables and how each is kept constant
Enough data: a sensible range, at least five values of the independent variable and repeats
Safety issues (high voltage, lasers, hot liquids, radioactive sources) addressed

criteria.name: Data analysis
look: Raw data tabulated with units, instrument uncertainties and consistent significant figures
Processing shown with a worked example, including propagation of uncertainties
A linearized graph with error bars, best-fit line and max/min gradient lines
Gradient and intercept interpreted physically, each with its uncertainty

criteria.name: Conclusion
look: A conclusion that answers the research question using the processed results
Comparison with the theoretical model or an accepted value, including percentage error
Judges whether the discrepancy lies within the experimental uncertainty
Recognizes the limits of the range over which the conclusion holds

criteria.name: Evaluation
look: Specific weaknesses identified, with their effect on the results (e.g. a non-zero intercept)
Clear distinction between random and systematic errors
Realistic improvements tied to each weakness, not just 'more repeats'
Thoughtful extensions that would test the model further

checklist: Research question states both variables, the range investigated and the system studied
Every measuring instrument has a stated uncertainty and justification
At least five values of the independent variable, each repeated
One full worked example of each calculation, including uncertainty propagation
Graph is linearized where the theory allows, with error bars on the points
Maximum and minimum gradient lines drawn and used to find the gradient uncertainty
Gradient and/or intercept linked to a physical quantity and compared with theory
Systematic errors discussed using the intercept or deviation from expected values
Improvements are specific to your apparatus and method
Report is under 3,000 words and sources are referenced consistently

examTips: Write the equation, substitute with units, then give the answer to sensible significant figures: method marks are available even if the final number slips.
Use the data booklet actively, but know what each symbol means and when an equation applies (e.g. suvat only for constant acceleration).
For 'explain' questions, chain the physics: cause → mechanism → effect, naming the law or principle you are using.
Read graphs carefully: check axis units and powers of ten, and decide whether you need the gradient, the area or an intercept.
Be precise with vectors and signs: state directions, choose a positive direction, and never add magnitudes of vectors at an angle.
